title: Lift-constrained trailing-edge noise control of a wing section: code and data
description:
Code and data for the paper Lift-Constrained Trailing-Edge Noise Control of a Wing Section: Achievable Authority and the Role of Aeroacoustic Model Form, Aerospace Science and Technology (accepted, 2026).

Every number, figure and table in the paper is produced by something in this archive, from the data also in it. The study asks how much trailing-edge self-noise a two-segment wing section can shed while holding the lift the flight condition demands, and answers it in resolved flow rather than through a semi-empirical chain. The answer is negative: the authority is absent at both lift conditions examined. A constraint-control framework that holds lift to a prescribed band under unknown bounded disturbances is reported alongside it, and is independent of that result.

Contents: the Brooks-Pope-Marcolini self-noise model in reduced and complete form, the Gaussian-process aerodynamic surrogate and its training set, two-dimensional steady k-omega SST solutions with a three-level grid-convergence study, four constraint control laws with a 2000-trial Monte-Carlo campaign, and a processor-in-the-loop package for an STM32F767ZI.
